slots.title: Japan core inflation 2.2% in October
slots.body:
Japan’s October core inflation print: **2.2%** year over year.

That’s below the **2.3%** consensus economists in a Reuters poll had been looking for.

Headline inflation came in at **2.3%**, up from **2.1%** in September.

Coverage tied the release to expectations that the Bank of Japan could move interest rates again, after core prices excluding fresh food picked up through the year.

Overnight, Japan’s main stock benchmark finished down **4.7%** at **56,668.30**, with reports citing pressure on chip and metals names after U.S. indexes slid in the prior session.

How much do overseas inflation prints shape what you watch at home before the U.S. open?

slots.title: Fed regional banks cap raises at 1%
slots.body:
The Fed’s 12 regional banks are planning **1%** annual raises for employees in the year ahead.

That compares with **3%** raises this year, according to reporting on the central bank’s push to rein in costs and streamline operations.

The story lands the same week two Fed officials are on the calendar to speak on **Nov. 20**: Christopher Waller at **1:25 p.m.** ET and Lisa Cook at **5:15 p.m.** ET.

In the prior U.S. session, the fear gauge moved up with equities lower:

- $^VIX +15.8% to **28.44**
- $^GSPC -2.0% to **7,175.83**

Do you treat Fed staffing and cost decisions as background noise, or as a signal about how the institution is run?

slots.title: BJ’s Wholesale reports on $1.26 EPS view
slots.body:
$BJ reports Nov. 20.

The Street’s EPS estimate is $1.26.

Revenue is estimated at about $5.97 billion.

The print measures how members are shopping at the warehouse-club chain — ticket size, traffic, and margin — not just one-day stock action.

$WMT already posted this week: EPS $0.65 vs a $0.64 estimate and revenue near $188.8 billion.

BJ’s number is smaller, but the same question: are consumers still stocking up in bulk?

Results typically land with the release; check the date on your earnings calendar.

What do you watch first on a club retailer report — comps, membership, or guidance?

slots.title: Moog set for $2.68 EPS on Nov. 20
slots.body:
$MOG-A earnings are on the calendar for Nov. 20.

EPS estimate: $2.68.

Revenue estimate: about $1.12 billion.

Moog makes motion-control systems — the kind of components that show up in defense, aircraft, and industrial equipment supply chains.

The release is a backlog-and-order snapshot as much as a quarterly EPS line.

No outcome is in the data yet; only the estimates and the date.

That’s what resolves when the report drops.

Do you follow small-cap industrials for order trends or mainly for the EPS print?
